hard_constraints: Korda escapes via a prepared lockdown/diversion; Ben and Talon capture a physical proof object (restricted field authorization, courier cylinder, or Foundation/Greyline transfer record) that names Iresh as the destination.

The GA restricted-transit placard is the single concrete object explaining why Ben cannot call Dorrin to lock down the space. No additional exposition about Coruscant's post-war logistics architecture.
Ben's exits-and-angles scan runs automatically, a Jacen-derived habit he does not reflect on in the moment.
Korda's prepared escape implies he expected this follow-through; he treats Ben and Talon as proficient.
The physical proof object is the first artifact that cannot be explained as coincidence: Korda is guarding an active operation, not a dead file.
No new plot mythology, no theme-as-thesis, no making Iresh abstract before it is physically clear.
Preserve commercial readability: goal, obstacle, movement, reversal, hook.
Use Character Voice & Life Sheet v1.4 as controlling source for dialogue, behavior, humor, fear, wounds, and interaction rules.
canon_risks: The GA restricted-transit logistics license and Verity district cargo-lane architecture are invented for this novel. Ensure they are described as post-war reconstruction infrastructure, not as a pre-existing Legends institution. No contradiction with known Legends Coruscant geography (e.g., the Verity district is not named in published Legends; treat it as a minor district that fits the post-war texture).
Korda's escape must not imply Force use or Sith training. He is a non-Force-sensitive former GAG security lieutenant using conventional security tradecraft.
Ben's automatic exits-and-angles scan must be shown as a Jacen-derived habit, not a Jedi technique. It is crisis logic, not a Force power.
legends_continuity_notes: Coruscant's post-war reconstruction after the Yuuzhan Vong War (25-29 ABY) and the Second Galactic Civil War (40-41 ABY) included extensive re-licensing of cargo lanes and transit corridors. The GA Logistics Oversight Bureau is a plausible post-war institution; it fits the 'return to normalcy' texture of the Dorvan administration.
The Verity district is not a named location in published Legends. It can be treated as a minor commercial/archive district on Coruscant, consistent with the planet's urban sprawl.

GAG-era security tradecraft (camera-lag patterns, prepared escape routes, false emergency lockdowns) are consistent with Korda's background as a former GAG security lieutenant. No Force involvement needed.
possible_disney_bleed: Avoid any reference to 'First Order', 'Resistance', 'Starkiller Base', or sequel-trilogy institutions.
Avoid 'Inquisitorius' as a post-Imperial organization (Legends Inquisitorius is Empire-era only).
Avoid 'kyber bleeding' or any Disney-canon lightsaber crystal lore.
Avoid 'World Between Worlds' or any Disney-canon Force concept.
Avoid 'Mandalorian' conventions from Disney+ (e.g., 'The Way'). Legends Mandalorians follow Resol'nare.
required_context_for_drafter: The GA restricted-transit placard is the whole explanation for why Ben cannot call Dorrin. One beat, one consequence. No further exposition.
Korda's escape is a prepared contingency, not improvisation. He expected someone to follow the bait and read the route.
The physical proof object (restricted field authorization, courier cylinder, or transfer record) is the first concrete artifact that names Iresh as the destination. The operation is already moving.
Ben's automatic exits-and-angles scan is a Jacen-derived habit. He does not reflect on it in the moment. It will matter later (Ch 31 Glasswell rescue).
Korda's escape compresses the timeline. Whatever margin Ben thought he had is gone.

The Verity district loading bay is a commercial logistics space trying to look unremarkable. Sensory details: hydraulic fluid smell, courier droids on repeating loops, slightly too-clean signage, blue-and-white GA Restricted Transit placard.
allowed_au_divergences: The Verity district and its loading bay are invented for this novel.
The GA restricted-transit logistics license and the GA Logistics Oversight Bureau are invented for this novel.
Korda's prepared escape route and the specific lockdown/diversion mechanism are invented for this scene.
The physical proof object (restricted field authorization, courier cylinder, or transfer record) is invented for this novel.
open_questions: Is the Verity district's location on Coruscant consistent with the known geography of the planet? (No published Legends map names it; treat as a minor district.)
Does the GA Logistics Oversight Bureau appear in any published Legends source? (Not to my knowledge; treat as invented.)
What specific form does the physical proof object take? (Scene card allows restricted field authorization, courier cylinder, datapad, or Foundation/Greyline transfer record. Drafter's choice.)

Does Korda's escape route involve any named Coruscant location that might conflict with published Legends? (Avoid named districts like the Senate District, Uscru Entertainment District, etc. Keep it generic.)
